source_meta._title: Sculk sensors do not detect item frame / glow item frame interactions

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 20w51a in a single-player Creative-mode world. Use keyboard and mouse terminology below; if controls are rebound, use the bindings for Inventory, Use Item/Place Block, Attack/Destroy, and hotbar-slot selection. No commands, coordinates, seed, dedicated server, or additional players are required by the report.
preconditions: A launcher installation or profile for the exact Java Edition snapshot 20w51a is available.
Use a new or disposable single-player world so the setup can be placed in a quiet, uncluttered area.

Create the world in Creative mode. Creative mode is an execution convenience because the report does not prescribe a game mode and the required objects can be obtained without crafting or exploration.
Reserve four hotbar slots for a solid support block, an Item Frame, a Sculk Sensor, and one visibly directional test item such as an Iron Sword.
Choose an open area with a solid floor and enough space to see both the item frame and the sculk sensor simultaneously.
The observation subsystem must be ready before the first item-frame interaction because placing the item, rotating it, and removing it are three separate trigger actions.

steps.action: Start Minecraft using the installation configured for the exact snapshot 20w51a. Do not substitute the fixed version 23w06a or another release.
steps.success_cue: The main menu identifies the running game as Minecraft Java Edition 20w51a.

steps.action: Open Singleplayer, select Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, and create the world. Leave all unrelated world settings at their defaults.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player has spawned in a Creative-mode world and the surrounding terrain has rendered.

steps.action: Wait until nearby chunks are fully visible and movement responds normally before constructing the test setup.
steps.success_cue: Terrain is no longer visibly loading around the player and movement responds without loading pauses.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory using the Inventory control, whose default keyboard binding is E, and select the Search Items tab. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Template%3AControl/doc?utm_source=openai))
steps.exact_input: E, then left-click the Search Items tab
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory is open and its item-search field is available.

steps.action: Search for Stone and place one stack into hotbar slot 1. Stone is only the solid support block for mounting the frame; another full solid block may be used if necessary.
steps.exact_input: Type "stone" in the search field; move Stone to hotbar slot 1
steps.success_cue: Stone is visible in hotbar slot 1.

steps.action: Clear or replace the search text, search for Item Frame, and place the ordinary Item Frame into hotbar slot 2.
steps.exact_input: Type "item frame" in the search field; move Item Frame to hotbar slot 2
steps.success_cue: An ordinary Item Frame is visible in hotbar slot 2.

steps.action: Clear or replace the search text, search for Sculk Sensor, and place it into hotbar slot 3.
steps.exact_input: Type "sculk sensor" in the search field; move Sculk Sensor to hotbar slot 3
steps.success_cue: A Sculk Sensor is visible in hotbar slot 3.

steps.action: Clear or replace the search text, search for Iron Sword, and place it into hotbar slot 4. The report permits any item; a sword is chosen because its displayed orientation is easy to distinguish after rotation.
steps.exact_input: Type "iron sword" in the search field; move Iron Sword to hotbar slot 4
steps.success_cue: An Iron Sword is visible in hotbar slot 4, and at least one additional hotbar slot remains empty.

steps.action: Close the inventory and return to first-person world control.
steps.success_cue: The inventory is closed and the crosshair is visible.

steps.action: Select the Stone in hotbar slot 1, aim at an open patch of ground, and place one Stone block. Ensure at least one vertical side face of the block remains exposed and reachable.
steps.exact_input: Press 1; aim at the ground; right-click once
steps.success_cue: One Stone block stands above the ground with an exposed vertical face.

steps.action: Select the Item Frame in hotbar slot 2, center the crosshair on the exposed vertical side of the Stone block, and use the item once to attach the frame.
steps.exact_input: Press 2; aim at the Stone block's vertical face; right-click once
steps.success_cue: An empty Item Frame is visibly attached to the side of the Stone block.

steps.action: Select the Sculk Sensor in hotbar slot 3 and place it upright on the ground directly beside the Stone support block. Do not put wool or another block between the sensor and frame.
steps.exact_input: Press 3; aim at the top of the adjacent ground block; right-click once
steps.success_cue: The Sculk Sensor is standing on the ground adjacent to the support block, with unobstructed space between it and the Item Frame.

steps.action: Move to a position in front of the frame from which the crosshair can reach its center while the entire Sculk Sensor also remains visible. Then release all movement controls.
steps.exact_input: Use movement controls as needed, then release them
steps.success_cue: The centers of both the Item Frame and Sculk Sensor are visible, the frame is within interaction reach, and the player is stationary.

steps.action: Without moving, wait at least 4 seconds so vibrations and sensor activity caused by constructing or approaching the setup have time to finish before the tested interactions begin.
steps.exact_input: Wait at least 4 seconds without movement, jumping, attacking, or placing blocks
steps.success_cue: No setup-generated vibration particle is traveling toward the sensor, and the sensor has returned to its resting visual state.

steps.action: Select the Iron Sword in hotbar slot 4 and keep the crosshair centered on the empty Item Frame. Do not move closer after this point.
steps.success_cue: The Iron Sword is held in the active hotbar slot, the frame remains empty, and the player is stationary within interaction reach.

steps.action: Use the Iron Sword on the empty Item Frame exactly once to place it inside the frame. This is the first interaction that the observation subsystem must monitor.
steps.success_cue: The Iron Sword is visibly displayed inside the Item Frame.

steps.action: Remain completely stationary for at least 4 seconds before performing the rotation interaction. Do not place blocks, jump, attack, or click the frame during this interval.
steps.exact_input: Wait at least 4 seconds without input
steps.success_cue: The Iron Sword remains displayed in its initial orientation and the setup is ready for an independently observable rotation interaction.

steps.action: With the crosshair still centered on the displayed Iron Sword, use the Item Frame exactly once to rotate the displayed item by one increment.
steps.success_cue: The Iron Sword remains in the frame but is visibly angled differently from its initial orientation.

steps.action: Remain completely stationary for at least 4 seconds so the rotation interaction is temporally separated from the removal interaction.
steps.exact_input: Wait at least 4 seconds without input
steps.success_cue: The rotated Iron Sword remains displayed and the setup is ready for the removal interaction.

steps.action: Select an empty hotbar slot so the player's hand is empty. Keep the crosshair centered on the displayed item.
steps.exact_input: Press the number key corresponding to an empty hotbar slot
steps.success_cue: The player's main hand is empty, and the rotated Iron Sword remains displayed in the Item Frame.

steps.action: Briefly use the Attack/Destroy control exactly once on the displayed item to remove it from the Item Frame. Do not hold the button and do not click a second time, because an additional attack could break the now-empty frame.
steps.success_cue: The Iron Sword is no longer displayed, while the empty Item Frame remains attached to the Stone block.

steps.action: After the removal click, remain stationary and make no further interactions until the observation subsystem has completed its inspection.
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary, the Item Frame is empty and still mounted, and the adjacent Sculk Sensor remains visible to the observer.

stor.handoff_condition: Immediately after step 16 has inserted the Iron Sword into the frame, begin observing the adjacent Sculk Sensor. Keep the observation subsystem active while the executor performs the separated rotation at step 18 and removal at step 21, ending with the player stationary beside the still-mounted empty frame.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode. Creative mode is selected only to obtain and arrange the required objects deterministically without crafting or commands.

The report says only that the Sculk Sensor should be "nearby" and does not provide an exact distance. Placing it on the ground directly beside the frame's support block is a practical deterministic interpretation.
The report permits "any item." An Iron Sword is selected because its orientation is visually unambiguous when the item is rotated.

The issue title includes Glow Item Frames, but the formal Steps to Reproduce explicitly use an ordinary Item Frame. Glow Item Frames were introduced in snapshot 21w03a, after the recommended first affected version 20w51a, so this primary plan tests the ordinary Item Frame only. ([zh.minecraft.wiki](https://zh.minecraft.wiki/w/Java%E7%89%881.17/%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%91%E7%89%88%E6%9C%AC?variant=zh-tw&utm_source=openai))

There are three distinct trigger actions in the report. The trigger_step field identifies the first one, item insertion at step 16; rotation at step 18 and removal at step 21 are additional trigger actions that must be monitored during the same handoff.

source_meta._title: Sculk sensors are not activated upon filling composters

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft: Java Edition snapshot 20w51a in a new single-player Creative-mode world. A Superflat world is recommended only to provide a clear, level test surface; no seed or coordinates are specified by the report.
preconditions: The Minecraft Launcher is able to install and run historical Java Edition snapshot 20w51a; enable snapshots in the launcher's Installations settings if necessary.
Use an unmodified world without behavior-changing mods or data packs.
Use Creative mode so the Composter, Sculk Sensor, and Cake can be obtained without unrelated crafting or exploration.
Perform the test on dry, level ground with no wool blocks between the composter and sculk sensor.
Choose a test location without moving entities or other vibration-producing activity near the sculk sensor.
The instructions use the default E inventory key and right mouse button for Use Item/Place Block; use the equivalent bound controls if they have been changed.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation for Java Edition snapshot 20w51a and launch it. Do not select the fix version 23w06a.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is open and identifies the running version as 20w51a.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, create a new world, and set Game Mode to Creative. For the simplest test area, open More World Options and select the Superflat world type, then create the world. The Superflat choice is optional and is not a report requirement.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> More World Options -> World Type: Superflat -> Done -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player has loaded into a Creative-mode world and surrounding terrain is fully rendered.

steps.action: Find a dry, level area with at least two adjacent ground blocks. Ensure no wool blocks, water, moving mobs, pistons, doors, or other repeatedly active objects are close to the intended test blocks. Stand on the ground within placement and interaction reach of both target blocks.
steps.success_cue: Two adjacent ground positions are available, no moving entity is visible nearby, and the player can use both positions without needing to walk after setup.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Open the Search Items tab, select the search field, enter "composter", and move one Composter into an empty hotbar slot. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots at the bottom of the screen.
steps.success_cue: A Composter is present in one of the nine hotbar slots.

steps.action: While still using the Creative inventory Search Items tab, replace the search text with "sculk sensor" and move one Sculk Sensor into a different empty hotbar slot.
steps.success_cue: A Sculk Sensor is present in the hotbar alongside the Composter.

steps.action: Replace the Creative inventory search text with "cake" and move one Cake item into another empty hotbar slot. Close the inventory by pressing E or Esc.
steps.success_cue: The inventory is closed, and the hotbar contains a Composter, a Sculk Sensor, and a Cake.

steps.action: Select the Composter hotbar slot using its number key or the mouse wheel. Aim at the top face of the first chosen ground block and press the Use Item/Place Block control once; by default, this is the right mouse button.
steps.success_cue: An empty upright composter is placed on the test surface, with its open side facing upward.

steps.action: Select the Sculk Sensor hotbar slot. Aim at the top face of the ground block directly adjacent to the composter and right-click once. Keep the sensor dry and do not put wool between it and the composter. Direct adjacency is a deterministic interpretation of the report's requirement that the sensor be nearby and places the composter well inside the sensor's detection radius.
steps.exact_input: Right-click once with Sculk Sensor selected
steps.success_cue: A dry sculk sensor is positioned directly beside the empty composter on the same surface level.

steps.action: Without walking if both blocks are already within reach, select the Cake hotbar slot using its number key or the mouse wheel. Aim the crosshair at the open top or inner face of the composter, but do not use the cake yet. If repositioning is unavoidable, hold the Sneak control, Left Shift by default, while moving, then stop completely.
steps.exact_input: Select Cake; hold Left Shift while repositioning if movement is required
steps.success_cue: Cake is visible in the player's hand, the composter is targeted by the crosshair, and the player is stationary within interaction range.

steps.action: Remain completely stationary and do not interact with either block for at least three seconds. Continue only after any vibration particle from setup activity has disappeared and the sculk sensor's tendrils have returned to their resting state. This prevents block placement, footsteps, or the sensor's activation period from masking the test interaction.
steps.exact_input: Wait at least 3 seconds without moving or interacting
steps.success_cue: The sculk sensor is visibly idle, no vibration particle is traveling toward it, and the empty composter remains targeted or within immediate reach.

steps.action: With Cake still selected, aim at the composter's open top or inner face and press the Use Item control exactly once; by default, right-click once. Do not walk, jump, place another block, or perform another interaction immediately afterward.
steps.exact_input: Right-click once on the composter with Cake selected
steps.success_cue: The composter has just accepted the cake and its visible compost contents have increased from the empty state; no additional action has yet been performed.

stor.handoff_condition: The cake has just been inserted into the previously empty composter while the adjacent sculk sensor was idle. The player is stationary and has performed no subsequent action; begin observing the sculk sensor immediately.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode, world seed, coordinates, world type, or exact distance between the two blocks. Creative mode, a new Superflat world, and direct horizontal adjacency were selected as minimal deterministic setup choices.

The report says to "fill the composter with a cake." This plan interprets that as inserting one Cake into an empty composter so that its compost level increases, rather than repeatedly inserting cakes until the composter reaches its final full state.

If reproducing in later affected versions where the Sculk Sensor is not available in the Creative inventory, a version-compatible item acquisition method may be required. The recommended reproduction version, 20w51a, is used here according to the affected-version selection rule.

source_meta._title: Sculk sensors are not activated upon sheep being dyed

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 20w51a in a single-player Creative-mode world with cheats enabled. A flat world, Peaceful difficulty, default controls, and no mods or datapacks are recommended to reduce unrelated movement and vibrations, but the report does not explicitly require them.
preconditions: Launch Minecraft Java Edition 20w51a, the first version listed as affected; do not use fix version 23w06a for this reproduction.
Create or load a Creative-mode world with cheats enabled so the supplied /summon command can be executed and the required items can be obtained without crafting.
Use an open area with solid, level ground and enough room to place a sculk sensor and stand a few blocks away from it.
Keep unrelated moving entities away from the immediate test area so their movement does not activate the sculk sensor during setup.
Use a dye color different from the sheep's current wool color. This plan uses red dye and verifies that the summoned sheep is not already red before applying it.

steps.action: Enter the Creative-mode test world and wait for world loading to finish before interacting with anything.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain is fully rendered, the player can move normally, and commands or inventory actions respond without loading delay.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory using the inventory action, whose default key is E.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory interface is open and displays item-category tabs.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory's Search Items tab, identified by its compass icon, and select its search field.
steps.exact_input: Click the compass-shaped Search Items tab
steps.success_cue: A searchable list of Creative inventory items and a text search field are visible.

steps.action: Search for a sculk sensor, then place one Sculk Sensor into hotbar slot 1. The hotbar is the nine-slot row at the bottom of the inventory.
steps.success_cue: A Sculk Sensor is visible in hotbar slot 1.

steps.action: Clear the inventory search field, search for red dye, and place Red Dye into hotbar slot 2.
steps.success_cue: Red Dye is visible in hotbar slot 2 while the Sculk Sensor remains in slot 1.

steps.action: Close the inventory using E or Escape, then select hotbar slot 1 using the corresponding hotbar control.
steps.success_cue: The world view is visible and the player is holding a Sculk Sensor as the active item.

steps.action: Aim at the top surface of a solid ground block in the open test area and use the place/use-item action, whose default input is right-click, to place the sculk sensor.
steps.success_cue: One Sculk Sensor block is placed upright on the ground with open space around it.

steps.action: Move to a position approximately two horizontal blocks from the placed sensor, remaining on the same ground level. Stop moving while still able to see the sensor clearly.
steps.exact_input: Use movement keys such as W, A, S, or D
steps.success_cue: The player is about two blocks from the sensor, the sensor is clearly visible, and there is room at the player's position for the sheep to be summoned.

steps.action: Open in-game chat using the chat action, whose default key is T. The command must be run in the game world rather than a dedicated-server console.
steps.success_cue: The in-game chat input field is open and ready to accept a command.

steps.action: Enter the report's summon command exactly as written, including the leading slash and NBT, then press Enter. The sheep will be summoned at the player's current coordinates.
steps.success_cue: A living, unsheared sheep appears at the player's position and remains stationary because NoAI is enabled.

steps.action: Move approximately one block away from the sheep so that the player is no longer occupying the same space, then turn to face the sheep. Keep both the sheep and the sculk sensor visible if possible.
steps.exact_input: Use a movement key briefly, then move the mouse to face the sheep
steps.success_cue: The stationary sheep is within right-click interaction reach, and the sheep remains only a few blocks from the sculk sensor.

steps.action: Confirm visually that the sheep's wool is not red. If it is already red, choose another dye from the Creative inventory whose color differs from the sheep; otherwise continue with the prepared red dye.
steps.success_cue: The selected dye color is different from the sheep's current wool color, allowing the dye interaction to change the sheep's color.

steps.action: Select hotbar slot 2 using the corresponding hotbar control so that Red Dye is the active held item.
steps.success_cue: Red Dye is visible in the player's hand and its hotbar slot is highlighted as active.

steps.action: Without walking or performing other interactions, wait until the sculk sensor has finished reacting to all setup movement and is visibly inactive. Also ensure that no unrelated entity is currently moving near it.
steps.success_cue: The sensor is in its resting state rather than displaying an active vibration response, the NoAI sheep is stationary, and the player is standing still within interaction reach of the sheep.

steps.action: Keep the Red Dye selected, aim directly at the sheep, and apply the dye once using the use-item/interact action, whose default input is right-click. Do not move or perform a second interaction afterward.
steps.success_cue: The sheep's wool changes to the selected dye color, confirming that the dye interaction was successfully completed.

stor.handoff_condition: The sheep has just been dyed once while stationary near the placed sculk sensor, and the player has performed no subsequent movement or interaction. Begin observing the sculk sensor immediately.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode, world type, difficulty, or whether the test must be performed in single-player or multiplayer. Creative-mode single-player with cheats is selected as the simplest way to obtain the sensor and execute the supplied command.

The report says only that the sheep should be summoned 'nearby' and gives no exact sensor-to-sheep distance. This plan uses approximately two blocks, which keeps the sheep visibly adjacent to the sensor without altering the supplied summon command.
The report permits any kind of dye but does not identify a specific color. Red Dye is selected as a deterministic example, with an explicit check that it differs from the sheep's existing color.

The Creative inventory navigation details and the recommendation to wait for the sensor to return to its resting state are practical execution choices rather than explicit requirements from the report.

source_meta._title: Sculk sensors do not detect daylight detector mode switching

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition 21w05b in a single-player Creative-mode world. The instructions use the English (US) item names and default controls. No dedicated server or additional player is required.
preconditions: Launch exactly Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 21w05b, the first version listed as affected. Do not use the fix version 1.19 Pre-release 3.
Use a Creative-mode world so the required blocks can be obtained without unrelated crafting or exploration.
Find a quiet, level test area with two horizontally adjacent ground blocks and unobstructed air above them.
Keep moving entities and other vibration-producing activity away from the test area during the final interaction.
Do not place wool between the daylight detector and sculk sensor.
Use an empty hand for the final interaction so right-clicking cannot place or use an unrelated item.

steps.action: Start Minecraft Java Edition using the 21w05b installation or launcher profile.
steps.success_cue: The main menu displays Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 21w05b.

steps.action: Create a new single-player world in Creative mode, or open an existing Creative-mode test world in this version. No specific seed or world type is required by the report.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player is in a loaded world and can fly and access the Creative inventory.

steps.action: Wait for initial world loading to finish before building the test. Do not continue while nearby terrain is still appearing or player controls are unresponsive.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain is rendered and movement and inventory controls respond normally.

steps.action: Locate a level test location containing two horizontally adjacent ground-block top surfaces. Ensure there is no wool or other block occupying the space between the positions where the two test blocks will be placed.
steps.success_cue: Two adjacent placement positions are visible and both have empty air above them.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory interface is open.

steps.action: Use the Creative inventory search to obtain a Daylight Detector and put it in hotbar slot 1. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots at the bottom of the inventory.
steps.exact_input: Open the Search Items tab, enter "daylight detector", select the Daylight Detector result, and place it in hotbar slot 1.
steps.success_cue: A Daylight Detector is visible in the first hotbar slot.

steps.action: Use the Creative inventory search to obtain a Sculk Sensor and put it in hotbar slot 2. Leave hotbar slot 3 empty for the final interaction.
steps.exact_input: Replace the search text with "sculk sensor", select the Sculk Sensor result, and place it in hotbar slot 2.
steps.success_cue: A Sculk Sensor is in hotbar slot 2, and hotbar slot 3 contains no item.

steps.action: Close the inventory and return to normal first-person control.
steps.success_cue: The world view and crosshair are visible, with the prepared hotbar displayed at the bottom of the screen.

steps.action: Select the Daylight Detector in hotbar slot 1.
steps.success_cue: The Daylight Detector is outlined as the active hotbar item and is shown in the player's hand.

steps.action: Aim at the top face of the first chosen ground block and place the Daylight Detector.
steps.success_cue: A Daylight Detector is placed on top of the ground at the test location.

steps.action: Select the Sculk Sensor in hotbar slot 2.
steps.success_cue: The Sculk Sensor is outlined as the active hotbar item and is shown in the player's hand.

steps.action: Place the Sculk Sensor on the top face of the horizontally adjacent ground block, at the same vertical level as the Daylight Detector. The two placed blocks should directly border each other with no intervening block.
steps.success_cue: The Daylight Detector and Sculk Sensor are placed side by side and both are visible.

steps.action: Select the empty hotbar slot 3 so the player's main hand contains no item.
steps.success_cue: Hotbar slot 3 is selected and the player's hand is empty.

steps.action: Stop walking, jumping, placing blocks, or performing other actions. Wait until any response caused during setup has completely ended before testing the mode switch.
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary and the Sculk Sensor has returned to its resting, inactive visual state.

steps.action: Without changing position if the block is already within reach, move only the camera until the crosshair points directly at the Daylight Detector. If repositioning is necessary, move into reach and then wait again until the Sculk Sensor is inactive.
steps.exact_input: Move the mouse to aim; use movement controls only if the detector is out of reach.
steps.success_cue: The Daylight Detector is targeted by the crosshair, the player's hand remains empty, and the adjacent Sculk Sensor is inactive.

steps.action: Right-click the Daylight Detector exactly once with the empty hand to switch it between its normal and inverted modes. Do not perform another action after the click before handing off to observation.
steps.exact_input: Right Mouse Button (Use Item/Place Block), once
steps.success_cue: The Daylight Detector's top appearance changes, confirming that its mode was switched once while the Sculk Sensor was adjacent and inactive immediately before the interaction.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just right-clicked the Daylight Detector once with an empty hand, its mode has changed, and the adjacent Sculk Sensor was in its resting inactive state immediately before the click. Begin observation immediately without moving, clicking again, or placing another block.
uncertainties: The report specifies only that the Sculk Sensor should be "nearby" and gives no exact distance or orientation. This plan places it horizontally adjacent to the Daylight Detector as the simplest deterministic interpretation.

The report does not specify a world seed, coordinates, dimension, world type, or game mode. A single-player Creative-mode world and an arbitrary level location are used only to make block acquisition and placement deterministic.
The report does not prescribe how to obtain the blocks. Creative inventory acquisition is an operational choice and is not asserted to be a condition of the bug.
The report does not specify whether controls or language settings are customized. The listed inputs assume default controls and English (US) item names.

source_meta._title: Sculk sensors are not activated upon frogs laying frogspawn

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition 1.19 Pre-release 1 in a fresh single-player Creative, Peaceful, Superflat world with cheats enabled. Use a stationary player-relative command anchor to create a small water-and-land test area, two adult frogs, and one nearby sculk sensor. A dedicated server and multiple players are not required by the report.
preconditions: Install and select the exact affected version "1.19 Pre-release 1" in the Minecraft Launcher; do not use the fix version 23w06a.
The test world must permit commands. Creative mode with cheats enabled is used so the setup can be created without exploration or crafting.
Use an open, level area with enough room for a 5×5 water pool and a sculk sensor approximately 2 blocks beyond one edge of the pool.
Keep wool blocks and wool carpets out of the test area and out of the space between the pool and the sculk sensor, because wool can interfere with vibration transmission.
Use two newly summoned adult frogs so neither frog is subject to a previous breeding cooldown.
Use the bound control for Use Item/Place Block when the steps say to right-click; the default control is the right mouse button.

steps.action: Start the Minecraft Launcher, select the installation for Java Edition 1.19 Pre-release 1, and launch the game. Do not substitute a later affected version or the fix version.
steps.success_cue: The main menu is loaded and displays "Minecraft 1.19 Pre-release 1" as the running version.

steps.action: Create a fresh single-player test world. From the main menu choose Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, ensure commands or cheats are enabled, set Difficulty to Peaceful, open More World Options, select the Superflat world type, confirm the settings, and create the world.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Allow Cheats: ON -> Difficulty: Peaceful -> More World Options -> World Type: Superflat -> Done -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player has spawned in a new Creative-mode Superflat world and can execute commands.

steps.action: Wait for initial world loading to finish before building the test area.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain is fully rendered, the loading overlay is gone, and player input responds normally.

steps.action: Stand normally on a level grass block in an open area. Treat this position as the command anchor. Do not change the player's position until both frogs have been fed, because the following commands use coordinates relative to this position. Rotating the camera without walking is allowed.
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary on solid level ground with at least 10 blocks of unobstructed space around the anchor.

steps.action: Open in-game chat with T, enter the exact command including the leading slash, and press Enter. This replaces a 5×5 section of the ground east of the anchor with water source blocks.
steps.success_cue: A 5×5 pool of still water is visible. Its surface is level with the surrounding ground, it has land around its edges, and the blocks directly above the water are air.

steps.action: Without moving from the anchor, open chat, enter the exact command including the leading slash, and press Enter to place the sculk sensor on the ground beyond the pool.
steps.success_cue: One sculk sensor is visible approximately 2 blocks beyond the pool's east edge. Every part of the 5×5 pool is within approximately 6.4 blocks of the sensor.

steps.action: Without moving, open chat, enter the exact command including the leading slash, and press Enter to obtain the two slimeballs needed to breed the frogs.
steps.success_cue: The command reports that two slimeballs were given, and a stack of two slimeballs is present in the player's inventory.

steps.action: Place the slimeballs in the hotbar and select their slot. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots at the bottom of the screen. In a fresh inventory, the command will normally put the slimeballs directly into an available hotbar slot; press that slot's number from 1 through 9. If they are elsewhere, press E, drag them into a hotbar slot, close the inventory with E, and press the corresponding number.
steps.exact_input: 1-9; if necessary, E to open and close the inventory
steps.success_cue: A slimeball is shown in the player's hand and the slimeball hotbar slot has the active-slot outline.

steps.action: Without changing the player's position, open chat, enter the exact command including the leading slash, and press Enter to summon the first adult frog on the land beside the pool.
steps.success_cue: One adult frog is visible on the land immediately beside the pool.

steps.action: Without changing the player's position, open chat, enter the exact command including the leading slash, and press Enter to summon the second adult frog at a separate position beside the same pool.
steps.success_cue: Two distinct adult frogs are visible near the pool.

steps.action: Close chat and rotate the camera with the mouse until both frogs can be individually targeted. Do not press W, A, S, or D. Confirm that the slimeball remains selected.
steps.success_cue: Both frogs can be seen near the pool, and the player is still holding a slimeball at the original anchor position.

steps.action: Aim the crosshair at the first frog and press the Use Item control once; by default, right-click once. Do not repeatedly click.
steps.success_cue: Heart particles appear above the first frog, confirming that it accepted the slimeball.

steps.action: Aim the crosshair at the other frog and press the Use Item control once; by default, right-click once. Make sure this is the second frog rather than feeding the first frog again.
steps.success_cue: Heart particles appear above the second frog, and the two frogs enter their breeding interaction.

steps.action: Stop all player movement and item use. Allow the frogs to finish their breeding interaction without feeding them again or modifying the pool, sensor, or surrounding blocks.
steps.success_cue: The frogs have completed the mating interaction, remain near the prepared water, and no further player input is required to make one of them search for a frogspawn-laying position.

steps.action: Using camera rotation only, frame the water surface and the nearby sculk sensor in the same view if possible. Do not walk, jump, place blocks, break blocks, use items, or issue further commands.
steps.success_cue: The pool and sculk sensor are visible or can be checked with minimal camera rotation while the player remains stationary.

steps.action: Remain stationary and wait for the bred frog to select a valid water block and lay frogspawn. Watch for a frogspawn block to appear on the surface of the prepared pool. The instant the frogspawn appears is the reproduction trigger; do not perform another action afterward.
steps.success_cue: A frogspawn block has just appeared on top of a water block in the prepared pool, with the nearby sculk sensor still in place.

stor.handoff_condition: The bred frog has just placed frogspawn on the surface of the prepared 5×5 pool, the sculk sensor remains positioned nearby, and the player has not performed any follow-up action. Begin observation immediately at this state.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode, world seed, difficulty, world type, or whether it was tested in single-player or on a dedicated server. A fresh single-player Creative, Peaceful, Superflat world is selected as a deterministic practical setup rather than as a claimed requirement of the bug.

The report describes the sculk sensor only as "nearby" and gives no exact distance. The plan uses a fixed geometry in which every possible frogspawn position in the prepared pool is within the sculk sensor's documented 1.19 detection range.

The report supplies no exact commands. The /fill, /setblock, /give, and /summon commands are operational setup choices using Java Edition 1.19 identifiers; they are not commands copied from the report.

Frog movement and the time required for a bred frog to select a water block are controlled by entity AI, so the exact waiting duration cannot be made deterministic. The observable continuation condition is the appearance of frogspawn on the water surface.

The frogs may move and generate unrelated vibrations before frogspawn is laid. The player is therefore instructed to remain stationary and keep both the pool and sensor visible so the autonomous laying moment can be identified precisely.
